causes.what: The NAS that backs the db-01 primary storage has a latency spike (about 3-5 ms to about 32-36 ms) and an IOPS drop (about 1800 to about 850). That stalls db-01 disk I/O, slows queries, and causes the slow responses across the app and web tiers.

ruled_out: db-01 CPU, memory and filesystem (cpu 22%, mem 52%, data fs 62%)
network or switch fault (no icmp loss, and the pattern is not specific to one switch)
db replica (db-02) as a cause (not checked in detail)
evidence: nas-01 latency jumped from 5.05 ms at 17:33 to 32.9 ms at 17:34 and has stayed at 32-36 ms since.
nas-01 IOPS dropped from about 1990 at 17:32 to about 820 at 17:35.
db-01 io wait went from 6.3% at 17:33 to 51.8% at 17:34, about 1 minute after the NAS latency jump and a minute before the first alert.
db-01 slow queries are at 26/s, connections at 119, and replication lag at 3.6 s.
All 4 web and all 4 app Slow-response alerts fired at 17:35-17:37, after the NAS and db I/O change.

db-01 has the tag storage=nas-01, and the web and app alerts span hosts on both distribution switches and both hypervisors, which points to a shared backend (db-01) rather than a switch or hypervisor fault.
The NAS has no alert of its own, because its latency is below any threshold. It is the earliest change in the data.
